speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth under the shoe recycling programme by Sport Singapore (a) why are donated shoes designated for recycling to create running tracks found by the press not to be recycled as planned; and (b) what is the Ministry doing to strengthen oversight to ensure proper implementation of such programmes.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) how many second-hand shoes have been wrongfully misdirected and exported for overseas resale after being collected from the public for recycling into sports infrastructure, amidst the collaboration between Sport Singapore and Dow; (b) whether the collection contractor and subcontractors have clearly specified contractual requirements for the handling and disposition of shoes collected under the collaboration; (c) whether the contracts provide for liquidated damages; and (d) whether any criminal offences have been disclosed.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth besides the shoe recycling programme by Sport Singapore (a) whether there are any other programmes that the Ministry is collaborating with other partners to promote recycling and sustainability efforts; and (b) what are the Ministry's oversight measures over such partners to ensure that they achieve the programmes' intended objectives.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I also understand that there is a request made for clarifications to be taken collectively, after the Minister of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE) answers Question No 8 through to Question No 10 on today's Parliamentary Order Paper.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Other partners, such as BT Sports and Alba-WH, are also involved in the project and play various roles in the process chain.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Dow's role is to manage the integration of the respective roles and promote the use of safe and sustainable materials.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: SportSG promotes the use of these materials to install sports infrastructure and set up shoes collection points at its ActiveSG sports centres.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Alba-WH is the appointed collection partner responsible for collecting shoes and delivering them to BT Sports, which manages the facility to grind the recycled shoes into granules for use as building materials.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This facility is Singapore's first grinding facility, which is able to grind recycled shoes into granules for use as building materials.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It was set up by BT Sports with the assistance of a grant from Government.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: SportSG pays only for the recycled granules which it receives from this facility and uses it for installation at public sports facilities.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These bins were brought to and then sorted at Yok Impex's premises, before being sent to Alba-WH's warehouse for registering and weighing.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They were subsequently delivered to the grinding facility.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will share these learning points across other recycling projects that the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) and other Government agencies undertake in partnership with like-minded stakeholders keen to work on initiatives that protect our planet.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To date, Sir, the project has otherwise been running well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This initiative has also led to more environmentally friendly materials being used in the construction of our public sports infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We assure the public that MCCY and the Public Service remains committed to the Singapore Green Plan 2030 efforts to support the national sustainability agenda.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Dennis Tan, please move Question No 8; we will take the clarifications later.
